messages:
emma: Heads-up — Acme reported a sudden embeddings throughput regression on rw-embed-large-v2 last night around 02:10 UTC. Their dashboard shows vectors/sec drop from ~14k -> ~5k while tokens/sec stayed flat. p99 latency jumped from ~110ms to ~480ms. They saw no 5xxs but queue_depth climbed above 300 for their tenant.
jones_acme: Confirming from our side. No client payload changes (single short texts, concurrency ramped up to 40 for a nightly job). We started seeing throttling around 02:08 and it persisted until we routed traffic elsewhere.
ravi_eng_ml: Any variant/quantization fallbacks recorded? If they get routed to q4 variants it can change per-vector CPU/GPU work.
leo_eng_runtime: Pulled runtime logs for tenant=acme-corp. Relevant snippets around the incident window:
```
2026-03-12T02:08:11Z BatchScheduler WARN queue_size=312 action=fallback_to_sync reason=agg_token_threshold
2026-03-12T02:08:11Z BatchSizer WARN batch_dim_change_detected old=128 new=16 tenant=acme-corp
2026-03-12T02:08:12Z ServingWorker INFO gpu_util=97.6% kvcache_hit_rate=0.86
2026-03-12T02:08:14Z ModelRouter INFO route=rw-embed-large-v2 variant=q4_0 selected=false
```
leo_eng_runtime: TL;DR: scheduler moved to fallback_to_sync and batch dim collapsed to many tiny batches. GPU stayed very busy but throughput cratered because we lost batching efficiency and added serialization overhead.
maria_sre: Autoscaler didn't spin up more pods — the Dedicated pool for that tenant hit reservation_limit. No infra maintenance around that time.
opsbot: route_override event applied to tenant=acme-corp by emma at 02:18 UTC -> reroute to region-eu-2
jones_acme: When we retargeted to a different region with spare capacity vectors/sec recovered to ~13.5k within seconds. So capacity/routing is a likely contributor.
ravi_eng_ml: Another hypothesis — token-length distribution skewed heavily short, causing the packer to infer aggressive pack sizes that then fail under high concurrency. But logs show batch_dim shrank, which indicates the opposite: something in the batcher heuristic started favoring small micro-batches.
leo_eng_runtime: I reproduced locally against staging by blasting short single-text requests (concurrency 48). After ~60-90s queue_size grew and fallback_to_sync fired. Reproducer (async) I used:
```
# repro_async.py
import asyncio
import aiohttp

URL = 'https://staging.api.redwood/v1/embeddings'
HEADERS = {'Authorization':'Bearer STAGING_TOKEN', 'Content-Type':'application/json'}
PAYLOAD = {'model':'rw-embed-large-v2', 'input':'hi'}

async def send(session):
    async with session.post(URL, json=PAYLOAD, headers=HEADERS, timeout=10) as r:
        await r.text()

async def main():
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as s:
        tasks = [asyncio.create_task(send(s)) for _ in range(2000)]
        await asyncio.gather(*tasks)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    asyncio.run(main())
```
leo_eng_runtime: Notably, when I increased scheduler.max_batch_bytes in staging the fallback didn't trigger and throughput returned to ~12k vectors/sec. Also tried disabling the small-batch heuristic (`batcher.enable_microbatch_detection=false`) and saw similar recovery — so it's definitely triggered by the batcher heuristics under small-request high-concurrency patterns.
ravi_eng_ml: Quick thought: prefix/KV cache won't help much for independent short inputs. The main fix is smarter batching heuristics that account for concurrency and reservation limits. Also might add a minimum batch time window for small requests when queue_depth is rising.
emma: Customer is worried about billing because requests took longer; confirmed there were no auth or billing errors. We should provide a root-cause and mitigation steps.
leo_eng_runtime: Example admin patch we used in staging (do not copy/paste to prod without ops approval):
```
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood/internal/tenants/acme-corp/overrides \
  -H 'X-Admin-Token: **REDACTED**' \
  -d '{"scheduler": {"max_batch_bytes": 30000000, "min_batch_time_ms": 5, "enable_microbatch_detection": false}}'
```
jones_acme: We validated the override in staging — after bumping max_batch_bytes and min_batch_time_ms vectors/sec jumped from ~5k -> ~11.8k and p99 fell back under 200ms. They still see a small tail when concurrency spikes >80 but overall much better.
maria_sre: Proposed immediate mitigations:
- Apply per-tenant scheduler overrides for the affected tenants (during a low-risk maintenance window).
- Add an alert on fallback_to_sync rate per-tenant so SRE gets paged earlier.
- Small canary rollout of the adjusted batcher heuristic to 5-10% of traffic next week.
ravi_eng_ml: Long-term work items:
- Rework batcher heuristics to incorporate tenant concurrency, reservation_limit signals, and historical token histograms.
- Emit structured telemetry `batcher_mode_switch_reason` with discrete enum values so we can chart why the batcher switched modes.
- Unit tests for fallback thresholds and microbatch behavior.
leo_eng_runtime: Created tracker SERV-9124: "BatchScheduler microbatch fallback causing throughput regression for many-small-request workloads". Assigned to eng-runtime with eng-ml as reviewer. PR for telemetry + tests incoming.
emma: Action items for support/ops:
- Notify Acme with temporary mitigation (we can apply override and schedule canary rollout).
- Offer guidance to reschedule their nightly analytics as a short-term workaround.
- Share timeline for permanent fix and ETA for canary.
jones_acme: We moved the analytics job to a different window. Thanks for the quick triage. Please keep us posted about the prod override schedule.
ravi_eng_ml: I'll prototype heuristic changes this sprint and add the telemetry flag. Leo — can you add a replica-level counter for fallback_to_sync so we have per-replica signals? Also add dashboard panel for queue_size histogram.
leo_eng_runtime: Yep — adding counters and dashboard tile. Linking changes to SERV-9124 and will open a follow-up postmortem doc after canary.
maria_sre: Once prod override is applied we'll monitor fallback counts and latency for 24h. If stable we'll proceed with canary rollout.
emma: Thanks everyone. Leaving thread open until we close SERV-9124 and confirm canary stability. :thumbsup:
